key_insight: Laser post-treatment reduced wear rates by approximately 24% for detonation-sprayed coatings and 39% for gas-flame-sprayed coatings, with deposition-dependent changes in hardness and elastic modulus.
engineering_relevance: Laser post-treatment offers a route to improve the dry-sliding wear resistance of Ni–Cr–Fe–Si–B–C coatings on AISI 321 stainless steel.
method: Deposit coatings by detonation spraying and gas-flame spraying, then apply laser post-treatment.
Characterize microstructure and phases using SEM, EDS and XRD.
Compare mechanical and tribological properties using instrumented indentation and ball-on-disk testing.
evidence_signal: DS hardness increased from 1049.1 to 1206.1 HV, while wear rates fell from 1.939 to 1.465 × 10⁻⁴ mm³/(N·m) for DS and from 2.419 to 1.476 × 10⁻⁴ mm³/(N·m) for GFS.
watch_item: Laser treatment did not improve every mechanical metric: GFS elastic modulus decreased from 228.0 to 187.0 GPa, and the abstract does not establish performance beyond dry sliding.
paper_title: Effect of Laser Post-Treatment on the Microstructure, Mechanical and Tribological Properties of Detonation- and Flame-Sprayed Ni–Cr–Fe–Si–B–C Coatings
